$schema-note: Reusable cast registry per media/engine/CONTRACTS.md 'Person API'. `characters` maps a lowercase character key to a style object consumed by Person.of(name) — engine/build/build-player.mjs reads this file and injects its `characters` object as the global CHARACTERS on every dev/player page, so any story can say Person.of('krishna') instead of redefining him in cast.js. Each entry carries: `archetype` — the closest palette-preset name from archetypes.js (king, queen, prince, princess, warrior, brahmin, priest, villager, hunter) OR, when a character's defining nature is superhuman, the closest Person behaviour-subclass name from person.js (deity, sage, rakshasa); the exact style overrides (same key vocabulary as stories/winning-of-draupadi/cast.js: skin, skinShade, hairColor, hairstyle, garb, clothMain, clothAccent, crown/turbanColor, sash/scarf, ornaments, build, tilak, beard/moustache, dhotiLen, female, etc.); a one-line `grounding` citation (repo-relative path into the corpus the look is drawn from); and an optional `notes` field flagging features today's engine can't fully draw yet (extra heads/arms, non-human anatomy, unsupported vahana/mount rigs) so a future agent renders an honest simplification instead of silently guessing. A handful of style values here go beyond what cast.js uses today (garb:'forest', garb:'hide', hairstyle:'loose') — they are proposed vocabulary for wardrobe.js/archetypes.js; until implemented, treat them as a cue to add support and fall back to the nearest existing value (sari/dhoti, topknot) meanwhile. The first 15 entries (arjuna … shiva) are copied verbatim — same keys, same hex values — from stories/winning-of-draupadi/cast.js; everything after is new and forward-looking, each grounded in the corpus.

arjuna.notes: this entry is Arjuna's Ādi-Parva brahmin disguise (white cloth, ascetic topknot, no ornament) — see arjunaGroom for the post-svayaṃvara reveal look; for a Kurukṣetra-era Arjuna, override garb:'armor' and drop sacredThread-as-only-ornament.

arjunaGroom.notes: revealed/wedding look once his identity is known — modest gold, garland from Draupadī.

draupadi.notes: "Kṛṣṇā, the dark one" — crimson & gold bridal sari, agni-born (see story.json sources for the fire-birth episode).

kunti.notes: widowed queen-mother register — subdued ochre, veiled, low ornament count (contrast a young/married-queen preset, which would run brighter and more bejewelled).

karna.notes: sun-touched skin and gilded cuirass reference his solar birth and the kavaca-kuṇḍala (born-in armor and earrings) that Indra later begs from him.

krishna.notes: depicted here as a Yādava prince-guest at the svayaṃvara, not performing miracles on screen; for a Gītā or Kṛṣṇa-līlā film where his divinity is foregrounded, consider archetype:'deity' with an aura/flute cue instead of a plain prince preset.

bhima.notes: brahmin here reflects the svayaṃvara-arc disguise (dhoti, sacred thread, no armor/crown) shared by all five Pāṇḍavas at this point in the story, not caste — Bhīma is a kṣatriya prince and, in most of the epic, the mace-wielding strongman; for a forest-exile or Kurukṣetra scene use archetype:'warrior' with garb:'armor' and drop the disguise cues.

yudhishthira.notes: same brahmin-disguise register as Bhīma/Arjuna at the svayaṃvara; he is the eldest Pāṇḍava and rightful king — use archetype:'king' with garb:'royal' once he is crowned (post-Kurukṣetra) or during the Rājasūya.

nakula.notes: svayaṃvara brahmin-disguise register, matching his brothers.

sahadeva.notes: svayaṃvara brahmin-disguise register, matching his brothers; distinguished from Nakula only by the cooler violet clothAccent/sash.

drupada.notes: king of Pāñcāla — regal purple & gold, grey beard.

dhrishtadyumna.notes: fire-born prince of Pāñcāla, Draupadī's twin, born from the same sacrificial fire as she (see draupadi.md / the story's 'fire' scene).

vyasa.notes: the sage — matted bun, rudrākṣa mālā, ochre robe; author-narrator and grandfather figure of the whole epic.

priest.notes: generic officiant for the svayaṃvara fire-rite / wedding scenes; unnamed in the source text, so no character-specific grounding beyond the parva itself.

shiva.notes: flashback-vision register in this story (ash-pale, tripuṇḍra, crescent drawn in-scene) for Vyāsa's account of Draupadī's five prayers/five husbands boon.

rama.notes: standard iconographic form is two-armed, dark blue/green-black complexion, kirīṭa-mukuṭa crown as royal heir (rama.md line on Vaiṣṇava iconography); 'kirita' is a proposed crown value alongside the existing 'mukut'/'turban'/'tiara'. For the forest-exile stretch of the Rāmāyaṇa, drop the crown/ornaments and switch garb:'dhoti' with matted hair instead.

sita.notes: no single fixed iconographic complexion for Sītā in this corpus's file; using the same warm-gold register as Draupadī/Kuntī since she is a princess-queen, not divine-blue like Rāma. Furrow-born/earth motifs (Janakī) suit gold+earth-tone accents in set dressing.

lakshmana.notes: devoted younger brother who follows Rāma into exile; for the 14-year forest stretch switch garb:'dhoti', ornaments:0 to match Rāma/Sītā's ascetic register.

hanuman.notes: vānara (monkey) anatomy — muzzle/snout face, fur-covered body, prehensile tail, long simian arms — is NOT supported by the current humanoid person.js rig. Until a dedicated vānara body-plan exists, this entry approximates him as the human warrior rig in a vermilion/orange palette (his sindoor association); prefer distant/silhouette poses or a tail add-on sprite over close-up faces that would expose the missing snout. Kapidhvaja (monkey banner) makes him a natural addition to any Arjuna-chariot scene.

ravana.notes: Daśagrīva — ten heads, twenty arms (Rām. Uttara-kāṇḍa 9) — well beyond the current one-head/two-arm person.js rig. For the multi-head reveal, composite several drawHead() calls fanned behind the primary head rather than quietly rendering him single-headed; for ordinary dialogue shots a single crowned, fanged head is a reasonable simplification as long as it isn't the 'true form' beat. tilak:'tripundra' nods to his long Śiva-devotion (Kailāsa episode, ravana.md). No fixed complexion is given in this corpus file; the bronze tone here is an iconographic convention, not a scriptural detail.

duryodhana.notes: deep-red/gold Kaurava court palette, deliberately distinct from the Pāṇḍavas' cream/pale tones. Signature weapon is the gadā (mace), trained under Balarāma; the vastraharaṇa thigh-slap gesture and the later Śalya-Parva thigh-wound (see duryodhana.md) are the two staging beats most likely to be dramatized.

bhishma.notes: white hair/beard and grey-steel armor for the aged patriarch-general most scenes depict (he took his celibacy vow young but nearly all epic action is decades later). Icchā-mṛtyu elder; the śara-śayyā (bed-of-arrows) death scene needs a reclined/impaled pose with no current POSES preset — likely a bespoke JS scene fn rather than a storyboard beat.

drona.notes: rāja-guru who takes up arms against his own brahmin caste norm; base look is the teacher (dhoti, sacred thread). For his Kurukṣetra command of the Kaurava host, override garb:'armor' with a gold-on-white palette to mark the generalship without losing the brahmin identity.

ganga.notes: iconographically fair-skinned, crowned, holding a water-lily/kalaśa. Her vāhana is the makara (crocodile/fish hybrid) — not among the props.js fauna rigs (drawHorse/drawElephant/drawDeer/drawBird/drawCow); represent her via flowing-water motifs and the riverBank set instead of a mount rig until a makara rig exists. hairstyle:'loose' is proposed vocabulary (see $schema-note).

shakuntala.notes: foundling raised wholly in Kaṇva's forest hermitage — garb:'forest' (bark-cloth/valkala) is proposed vocabulary; wardrobe.js doesn't define it yet, so fall back to garb:'sari' with a desaturated ochre palette and ornaments:0 meanwhile. Switch to garb:'royal', ornaments 2+ for her later Hastināpura court scenes as Duṣyanta's queen.

savitri.notes: "sheds her royal ornaments, dons bark-cloth" to serve her ascetic in-laws (MBh Vana Parva 293) — same garb:'forest' proposed value as Śakuntalā. She is Aśvapati's princess before choosing Satyavān, so a pre-marriage svayaṃvara-quest scene should use garb:'royal' with ornaments restored.

yama.notes: dark storm-cloud/green complexion, blood-red robe, majestic-kingly in benign depictions (yama.md). Vāhana is a black water-buffalo (Mahiṣa) — props.js has drawCow but no drawBuffalo; approximate by re-palette-ing drawCow darker with larger horns until a dedicated rig lands. Carries a daṇḍa (staff) and pāśa (noose) as held props, neither currently in the props.js list.

bakasura.notes: the man-eating rākṣasa of Ekacakrā whom Bhīma kills in the brahmin's place (Ādi 159-166, cited at adi-parva.md lines ~66/72); garb:'hide' is proposed vocabulary for wild rākṣasas with no royal dress (cf. Hiḍimba in hidimba-hidimbi.md for the same register). Do not confuse with the crane-demon Bakāsura that infant Kṛṣṇa kills at Vraja (Bhāgavata Purāṇa X.11, see 04-deep-dives/vraja-boyhood-demons.md) — a distinct character sharing the name.

hidimba.notes: a kāmarūpiṇī (shape-shifter) — this palette is her chosen beautiful-human-woman guise (Ādi Parva ~154-155), styled close to Draupadī/Kuntī's warm tones but in forest green rather than court color. Some tellings say 'Hiḍimbā/Hiḍimbī' for her and reserve 'Hiḍimba' for the cannibal brother Bhīma kills; the same source file covers both, disambiguate by context. A true-rākṣasī-form variant (yellow eyes, tusks, per her brother's description in the same file) could be added if a scene needs it.

ganesha.notes: elephant head (trunk, large ears, single/broken tusk) and a pot-belly are the defining silhouette — person.js's human drawHead()/drawFigure() proportions can't produce these from a palette swap alone; needs a dedicated head-variant and body-proportion override, tracked as an engine gap, not just a style override. Vāhana is a mouse (Mūṣika) — no rodent rig exists in props.js yet either.

durga.notes: Devī Māhātmya iconography is eight-/ten-/eighteen-armed (popular Mahiṣāsura-mardinī form has ten, Daśabhujā), each hand holding a different god-given weapon, mounted on a lion. person.js currently rigs one pair of arms and props.js has no drawLion; for a faithful tableau either extend the rig for multi-limb compositing or stage her with 2-4 held weapons and flag the reduction rather than pretending it's the full iconography.

lakshmi.notes: Śrī Sūkta calls her golden-hued (hiraṇya-varṇām), lotus-seated and lotus-garlanded (padma-mālinīm) — render the lotus seat/garland as set-dressing/props, not character-style keys. Some traditions show her four-armed (lotus, pot, abhaya, varada mudrās); default to two-armed with a held-lotus prop unless a scene calls for the fuller iconography, same caveat as Durgā.
